query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an α + β dual-phase alloy with low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Earlier studies explored redesigning the bulk alloy, which risks compromising its original advantages, and several surface-modification approaches. Traditional thermal spraying and thermal plating produced weak coatings with poor substrate bonding; composite coatings suffered from uneven constituent dispersion and weak interfaces; and laser cladding could generate intermetallic compounds, high residual stresses, cracks, and crazing. Prior refractory high-entropy-alloy studies reported improved hardness and wear resistance, but the broader requirements of compositional homogeneity, strong bonding, mechanical stability, and preservation of TC4’s beneficial properties remain. Formulate one neutral, testable hypothesis for an intervention that could satisfy these requirements. Specify the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The application of a FeCoNiCrMo0.2 + WC + CeO2 CHEA coating on the surface of TC4 alloy, with optimized laser cladding parameters and composition, will result in improved hardness and wear resistance, with a predicted increase in hardness of 20% and a decrease in wear rate of 30% compared to the untreated TC4 alloy.
generation.intervention: Laser cladding of a FeCoNiCrMo0.2 + WC + CeO2 CHEA coating with a thickness of 500 μm and a composition of Fe-20Co-20Ni-20Cr-20Mo0.2 + 20WC + 2CeO2 (at.%) on the surface of TC4 alloy
generation.conditions: Laser cladding parameters: laser power of 2 kW, scanning speed of 5 mm/s, and a defocus distance of 10 mm; the substrate is pre-heated to 500°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a uniform hardness distribution and a stable friction coefficient in the CHEA coating
generation.mechanism: The CHEA coating enhances the hardness and wear resistance of the TC4 alloy by forming a uniform and stable microstructure, which resists plastic deformation and crack propagation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and wear resistance of the TC4 alloy, with a predicted increase in hardness of 20% and a decrease in wear rate of 30% compared to the untreated TC4 alloy
generation.boundary: The coating process is optimized to mitigate the risk of uneven distribution of hard phase particles in the coating microstructure
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in hardness and wear resistance may vary depending on the specific coating process and material properties

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment with a untreated TC4 alloy sample and a sample with the optimized CHEA coating, subjected to the same wear and friction tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized CHEA coating does not result in a significant improvement in hardness and wear resistance compared to the untreated TC4 alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

To further improve the properties of this coating, FeCoNiCrMo high entropy alloy (HEA) coatings, and two composite coatings, FeCoNiCrMo0.2 + WC and FeCoNiCrMo0.2 + WC + CeO2, were prepared on the surface of 316L stainless steel by laser cladding technology. After adding WC ceramic powder and CeO2 rare earth control, the microstructure, hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance of the three coatings were carefully studied. Zhang et al. [] prepared a composite powder coating of TC4 and WC on the surface of TC4 titanium alloy. The results showed that adding 5%, 10%, and 15% WC content could help improve the microhardness and wear resistance of the coating, and the coating forming quality was good without cracks and other obvious defects. Chong et al. [] added 5% WC into AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy powder, and the research showed that WC enhanced the hardness of the AlCoCrFeNi coating, reduced the surface roughness, and improved the wear and corrosion resistance. Hu et al. used high-speed laser cladding to prepare a Ni/WC composite powder coating. The research showed that WC improves the microhardness and wear resistance of the coating and can refine the grain structure, and the decomposition of C and W elements precipitated from the coating played a solid solution strengthening role. Ma et al. [] studied the microstructure, microhardness, and wear resistance of a 60% WC-reinforced FeCoNiCr composite coating prepared by laser cladding. The results showed that the composite coating had good forming quality and better microhardness and wear resistance.

Conversely, excessive CeO2 can hinder the refinement of the microstructure and the improvement of microhardness, thus slightly reducing the wear resistance of the coating []. Gao et al. [] studied the effects of CeO2 addition on crack sensitivity, microstructure, phase composition, solute segregation, and microhardness of the Ni60 cladding layer.
